Environment: Python 3.14.3, fresh venv at /tmp/venvB, `pip install -e ".[dev]"`. No warnings, no skips, no xfails. Source: 1573 lines across src/; tests: 1959 lines. Not a git repository, so commit count and bisectability could not be measured.
unanticipated_findings: REPRODUCED: `replay --id N` re-invokes the handler on a delivery that is already `processed`, with no guard, no warning, and exit code 0 — silently doing exactly the duplicate work the whole system exists to prevent. src/webhook_receiver/service.py:177-182 (`_run_handler`) fetches the delivery and calls the handler without ever inspecting `delivery.status`, and src/webhook_receiver/cli.py:146-148 loops over the selected deliveries calling it. Repro: after one successful delivery, `cli.main(['replay','--id','1'])` printed `1  acme  ok` / `1 reprocessada(s), 0 falhou(aram).` and exit 0, while the DB went from `attempts: 1, handler_events rows: 1` to `attempts: 2, handler_events rows: 2` (status stayed `processed`). The same hole exists for `replay --status received`: nothing claims or leases a delivery, so an operator replaying a `received` delivery races the in-flight BackgroundTask for that same id and both can run the handler. The `--dry-run` output does show the current status, but nothing blocks or warns on execute.

Production code carries a test-only global mutable hook: src/webhook_receiver/service.py:45-51 defines `_before_reserve` and `set_reserve_barrier()`, a process-wide callable invoked on every accepted delivery at service.py:99-100. It exists solely for the concurrency test at tests/integration/test_http.py:194-231. If it is ever left set (an exception between set and the `finally` reset, or any other caller), every request in the process silently runs foreign code between key resolution and reservation.

The `content_hash` dedup fallback derives its key from sender + signature timestamp + body (src/webhook_receiver/idempotency.py:26-30), so it does not dedup the case it exists for. Real senders re-sign each retry attempt with a fresh timestamp; the same event retried one second later yields a different derived key and is accepted as a brand-new delivery, invoking the handler again. It only catches byte-identical replays, including the identical timestamp header. The README mentions the false negative in one line, but config/senders.example.toml ships the `globex` sender on exactly this mode, so the shipped example has effectively no retry protection for that sender.

`PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL` under WAL (src/webhook_receiver/schema_sqlite.py:13) means a transaction that has COMMITted — and therefore already produced a 202 to the sender — can be lost on OS crash or power loss (it is durable only across process crashes). The README's durability claim ('persiste a entrega antes de responder') and the enumerated loss cases in 'A promessa de entrega' do not mention this window, so an operator reading the docs would not know that an acknowledged delivery can vanish.

`/healthz` can report `{"status":"ok"}` for up to 5 seconds after the database has actually become unwritable: src/webhook_receiver/db.py:138-166 caches the writability verdict in a module-level `_health_cache` dict. The 5s TTL is a documented deliberate trade-off against lock contention, but the cache is also unbounded (one entry per DB path, never evicted) and shared by every app instance in the process, so two apps on the same path inherit each other's verdict. tests/unit/test_store.py:14 has to call `db._health_cache.clear()` to work around this.

The README has two sentences truncated mid-clause: 'A forma completa das respostas, do CLI e do log está em' (ends there, no destination) and 'Mudanças que toquem verificação, deduplicação ou o momento da resposta precisam' (ends there, no requirement). It also says 'Detalhes, invariantes e arestas conhecidas estão no mapa de arquitetura', but no such document exists anywhere in the artefact — the only other prose files are CHANGELOG.md and LICENSE.

Build artefacts that .gitignore explicitly excludes are shipped inside the artefact directory: `webhooks.db` (28 KB, containing a real `deliveries` row with `idempotency_key='entrega-1'`, raw_body `{"event":"pedido.criado","id":7}`, plus one `suppressions` and one `handler_events` row), `.coverage` (90 KB), and `.pytest_cache/`. `config/senders.toml` is also present despite being gitignored; it is byte-identical to config/senders.example.toml, so no secret is exposed, but the state DB from a prior run is real data leaking into the deliverable.
